title: operator MFA validation, KMS key-usage telemetry and residency-tag enforcement
author: Priya R. Sharma
description:
Motivation: tighten operator session surface and telemetry for KMS usage while making region/residency violations detectable and actionable. This PR implements three coordinated changes: 1) server-side enforcement that elevating operator actions (role grants, policy changes, operator impersonation) require an active MFA assertion on the operator session; 2) lightweight per-key KMS usage telemetry (aggregated counters + tenant affinity) and a Grafana dashboard so platform + security teams can audit KMS access patterns; 3) request-time validation of residency/region tags for KMS-bound operations to reject calls that would cross a tenant's region pin or configured residency constraints.

What changed (high level): added an MFA-check middleware and an operator-privilege gating hook; enriched audit events with mfa_result and location_assertion fields; plumbed per-key telemetry events into the telemetry pipeline with an efficient aggregator; added a residency-tag validator to the KMS request path and failing fast with clear audit reasons; simple Console UI link to the new "Policy explainer" and a one-click jump to KMS usage for that key.

Files of note and rationale (single-string summary): all code changes are backwards-compatible for normal user flows; operator-level APIs now return 403 when MFA is missing for elevated paths. We intentionally do not roll MFA into token issuance here to avoid large-scale invalidation - this is an enforcement shim on elevated endpoints only. Telemetry uses existing metrics ingestion with a small new label "kms_key_id" and uses cardinality limits per-tenant to avoid explosion. Residency validation consults the tenant metadata cache and rejects calls where the key/provider does not satisfy the tenant's residency policy.

Checklist:
- [x] MFA middleware and unit tests
- [x] Audit enrichment and integration tests
- [x] KMS telemetry producer + dashboard (grafana json)
- [x] Residency validator unit + integration tests
- [x] Console link and docs stub
- [x] Performance microbenchmarks (latency impact < 3ms p50 on KMS proxy path)

Testing & verification: added targeted unit tests (service/auth, service/audit, service/kms) and an end-to-end integration test that simulates operator session without MFA attempting an elevated change (assert 403 + audit event contains mfa_result: "missing"). Telemetry smoke tests validate per-key counters increment and are visible on the new Grafana panel. Load test on staging (10k TPS mixed workload) shows <2% CPU increase on KMS proxy fleet and <3ms median added latency.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind config.security.operator_mfa_enforce (default: off). We will enable in a staged rollout: tenant pilot -> orgs with strict compliance -> global. Telemetry and residency enforcement are safe to enable globally but we will watch dashboards for unexpected 403 spikes.

Operational notes & migration: no token format changes. Ops should watch the new dashboard and the audit stream (location_assertion, mfa_result). If a tenant sees unexpected rejections set config.security.operator_mfa_enforce=false while investigating.

Known limitations: policy explainer in Console links to effective-policy view but does not yet simulate cross-tenant delegations (follow-up ENG-5643). Telemetry currently exposes only counters and does not retain raw per-call samples (by design, to limit PII).

References: Linear ENG-5491, SEC-302 for threat model; internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/mfa-kms-residency (doc stub).

review_comments: Luca Moretti (review): Please add a latency microbenchmark for the residency check path — what happens when tenant cache is cold?
Priya R. Sharma (author): Added a microbenchmark in service/kms/proxy/bench_test.go and clarified cache warmup behaviour; cold-cache adds ~1.8ms median (measured on staging) — included in PR notes.
Aisha Khan (review): Telemetry cardinality: ensure tenants cannot create high-cardinality keys and blow up metrics. Can we limit tags?

Priya R. Sharma (author): Telemetry aggregator enforces per-tenant cardinality cap (config.telemetry.kms_cardinality_limit) and we drop/aggregate labels beyond the cap. Added tests that assert cap behaviour.
Daniel Park (review): We need to ensure audit log schema bump is backward compatible for downstream consumers.
Priya R. Sharma (author): Audit schema change is additive; consumers can ignore new fields. Added docs and a compatibility note in service/audit/README.md.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash on 2025-01-24 by Priya R. Sharma (merge method: squash). Commit message: 'security: enforce operator MFA on elevated paths; kms telemetry; residency validator'
release_notes: Security: operator-level MFA enforcement for elevated operations (feature-gated). Observability: per-KMS-key usage telemetry + Grafana dashboard. Compliance: tenancy residency/region-tag validation on KMS operations; rejecting violating calls with explicit audit reasons. Console: 'Policy explainer' quick-link. No public API breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: Watch grafana panel 'KMS / Key usage' and 'Audit / Operator MFA fails'. If 403 rate spikes after enabling, disable feature flag and investigate tenant metadata mismatches.
notes: This PR was intentionally scoped to enforcement and telemetry only. Follow-ups: simulation-mode rollout, simulator for policy explainer (ENG-5643).
